{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-tn","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"e396235e262cec9a28d1c5ce13863387d49282e1aa2eb910a866997176fe987c","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-tn-class-d:lineage:51","source_registry_sha256":"8b0b6a068a0aa720d419171b5007a2610ed6c5012eeff522b57713cf9226eb71","source_liveness_sha256":"d27b9a94f03ec29d960b8eea38966606a7d3fdb703ad30b19ecd93f9bc70d0c7"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Alcohol, other drugs and driving confusables and continuation details","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: where impaired drivers drink, body size, liver damage, eye effects, lower limits, medicine labels, officer stops, DUI offender IDs, seizure, felony child endangerment, added penalties, costs, young riders, designated drivers, prevention tips and dated statistics","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: where impaired drivers drink, body size, liver damage, eye effects, lower limits, medicine labels, officer stops, DUI offender IDs, seizure, felony child endangerment, added penalties, costs, young riders, designated drivers, prevention tips and dated statistics
Confusable pairs and continuation facts; each block ties to one manual page, and any hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A01
Of the drivers estimated to be intoxicated late at night, more than one-third had been drinking at someone else's home. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A01
A smaller person who tries to keep pace with larger friends' drinking will usually feel impaired judgment and lowered inhibitions sooner. [A01]
Why it matters: group body factors; confusable body weight versus body fat.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A01
The liver breaks down roughly 90 percent of the alcohol in the body, so a damaged or diseased liver keeps BAC higher for longer. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A01
Heavy, long-term drinking can harm nearly every organ, and its effect on the liver can lead to hepatitis and cirrhosis. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A01
An estimated two in every five Americans, or 40 percent, will be in an alcohol-related crash at some point in their lives. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0093]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A02
Alcohol relaxes the eye muscles so they cannot focus properly, which also makes glare vision poor. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A02
Alcohol makes each eye receive a slightly different picture, which throws off judgment of depth and distance and raises the risk of head-on and rear-end crashes. [A02]
Why it matters: group vision; confusable depth judgment versus side vision.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A02
The eyes supply almost 90 percent of the information a driver uses, so any loss of vision can be disastrous. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A02
As drinking increases, alertness and concentration fade while reaction time and coordination keep getting worse, a deadly combination behind the wheel. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A02
Lower legal alcohol levels apply to younger drivers, commercial drivers and repeat offenders than the general .08 level. [A02]
Why it matters: group limits; confusable general limit versus lower limits.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0094]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: A03
Alcohol slows all nerve impulses and body functions, which limits a driver's ability to stay alert and concentrate. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-R12 | anchor: A03
If your doctor prescribes a tranquilizer or sedative, ask how it will affect your ability to drive safely. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-R13 | anchor: A03
Watch for medicine label warnings such as may cause drowsiness or do not operate machinery, and ask a doctor or pharmacist about any drug or drug combination you are unsure of. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-R14 | anchor: A03
Studies show marijuana and other drugs also affect judgment and motor skills, so driving under their influence is dangerous too. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-R15 | anchor: A03
Erratic driving or a speed that is too fast or too slow is enough reason for an officer to stop a vehicle and investigate for DUI. [A03]
Why it matters: group DUI stops; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-R16 | anchor: A03
If a person whose license was revoked for DUI applies for a photo ID during the revocation, the department must mark the ID to show the holder is a DUI offender. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-R17 | anchor: A03
For a Tennessee resident, the DUI litter pickup is done in the offender's home county. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0095]

FACT_ID: sec12-R18 | anchor: A04
A vehicle can be seized when a driver whose privileges are already revoked for DUI is charged with driving on that revoked license. [A04]
Why it matters: group seizure; confusable revoked-license seizure versus repeat-conviction seizure.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-R19 | anchor: A04
Under the Drunk Driving Child Protection Act, a DUI that seriously injures an accompanying child is a Class D felony, and one that kills the child is a Class C felony. [A04]
Why it matters: group child endangerment; confusable injury versus death.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-R20 | anchor: A04
A judge will also order a drug and alcohol treatment assessment, with treatment as needed, for an offender who had a prior DUI within the five years before the current one. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-R21 | anchor: A04
Other court-ordered DUI requirements can include an alcohol safety DUI school where available, rehabilitation for second and later convictions, and restitution to injured victims when the offender can pay. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-R22 | anchor: A04
Beyond fines and court costs, a DUI can bring bond, attorney fees, lost work time, alcohol course and treatment fees and higher insurance premiums, adding up to several thousand dollars. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-R23 | anchor: A04
The DUI penalty table lists a first conviction as 48 hours in jail, or 7 days with a BAC of 0.20 percent or more, a fine of $350 to $1,500 and a 1-year revocation. [A04]
Why it matters: group penalty table; confusable first versus second conviction.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-R24 | anchor: A04
The DUI penalty table lists a second conviction as 45 days to 11 months and 29 days in jail, a fine of $600 to $3,500 and a 2-year revocation. [A04]
Why it matters: group penalty table; confusable second versus first conviction.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-R25 | anchor: A04
According to the DUI penalty table, a fourth or later DUI conviction is a Class E felony. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-R26 | anchor: A04
Traffic crashes are the leading killer of young people, and nearly half of those crashes involve alcohol. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0096]

FACT_ID: sec12-R27 | anchor: A05
Most teenagers become intoxicated at low BAC levels. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-R28 | anchor: A05
A second juvenile alcohol or drug conviction for someone aged 13 to 17 brings a suspension of two years or until age 18, whichever is longer. [A05]
Why it matters: group under-twenty-one laws; confusable first versus second juvenile offense.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-R29 | anchor: A05
Underage driving while impaired can also include public service work in addition to the license loss and fine. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-R30 | anchor: A05
The designated driver approach, where friends agree in advance who will stay completely sober, is one of the most successful recent programs, and many night clubs give that driver free non-alcoholic drinks. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-R31 | anchor: A05
Alcohol-related crashes are not accidents but preventable events, so decide before you start drinking that you will not drive, since the decision gets harder after a drink or two. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-R32 | anchor: A05
To avoid drinking and driving, go out in groups with a driver who agrees not to drink, ride with a sober friend, or hand your keys to a sober person before you start. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-R33 | anchor: A05
If someone offers you a drink and you plan to drive, simply decline and say you are driving. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-R34 | anchor: A05
Alcohol quickly reaches the brain and disrupts the parts that control judgment, emotions and confidence, and judgment is the first thing affected. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-R35 | anchor: A05
Reliable studies show that two or three drinks in three hours or less impair the driving of most people. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-R36 | anchor: A05
Alcohol-related crashes are the number one killer of people under age 40. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-R37 | anchor: A05
Cold medicines can make you feel well enough to drive while still dulling alertness, judgment, coordination and vision, and combining alcohol with antihistamines can be more dangerous than either alone. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-R38 | anchor: A05
In 2020, 326 Tennessee traffic deaths, or 27 percent, were alcohol-related, and 122 of them also involved a driver who had used drugs. [A05]
Why it matters: dated statistic; dynamic.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-R39 | anchor: A05
For 2021 the manual reports about 24 percent of fatalities as alcohol-related and about 41 percent as involving a driver impaired by drugs or alcohol. [A05]
Why it matters: dated statistic; dynamic.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-R40 | anchor: A05
Nationwide in 2020, 11,654 traffic deaths, about 30 percent of the total, were alcohol-related. [A05]
Why it matters: dated statistic; dynamic.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0097]

FACT_ID: sec12-R41 | anchor: A06
The chapter was written with the Tennessee Association of Alcohol, Drug and Other Addiction Services, and its toll-free Redline at 1-800-889-9789 offers information and referrals. [A06]
Why it matters: dynamic contact detail.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0098]

FACT_ID: sec12-R42 | anchor: A06
The sample questions at the end of the chapter are only study aids, and the real knowledge test may use entirely different questions. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0098]
